title: Visual hierarchy for a screen
when: A page or screen feels flat or busy and the user wants the important things to stand out in the right order.
inputs: the one action that matters most
prompt:
Goal: A screen where readers see the main message first, the main action second and details third, by choices you can name.
Steps:
1. Rank the content: write the top three things a visitor must notice, in order, before touching CSS.
2. Rank one gets the strongest size and weight, rank two the accent (the primary button), rank three plain body text.
3. De-emphasize instead of emphasizing more: muted secondary text, smaller labels, lighter borders.
4. Use position: rank one early on the reading path (F pattern for text pages, Z pattern for sparse sections).
5. Keep a full type step between levels and at most two signals (size, weight, color) on one element.
6. Squint test: zoom out to 25 percent; the ranking should survive.
Quality bar:
- One focal point per section.
- Accent only on actions and key data.
- Muted text still passes 4.5 to 1.
Pitfalls:
- Bold everywhere, so nothing is bold.
- Several accent colors.
- Decoration louder than content.
Verify:
- [ ] The ranking is in the reply.
- [ ] Rank one uses the largest heading.
- [ ] Only primary actions use the accent fill.
- [ ] Contrast passes.
Output: Updated style.css (and markup order if needed) plus the three line ranking in the reply.

examples.input: minha pagina parece baguncada, nada se destaca
examples.output: rank 1 h1 offer at step 5, rank 2 Book now accent button, rank 3 details in muted text
